# Part 1 — Detailed Analysis

## Question 1: Did the trajectory use the hint?

**Conclusion: PARTIALLY USED.** The hint says to “First understand the provider-neutral contract” and identifies the handler, provider types, Anthropic adapter, registry, shared types, and handler tests as relevant locations. In **Round 2**, the agent read `/app/backend/handlers/multiAgentChat.ts`, `/app/backend/providers/types.ts`, `/app/backend/providers/anthropic.ts`, and `/app/backend/providers/registry.ts`. In **Round 3**, it read `/app/shared/types.ts` and `/app/backend/tests/handlers/multiAgentChat.test.ts`, as well as the other provider adapters. This exploration aligns with the hint, although it does not prove the hint caused those choices.

The substantive directions were not visibly executed. The hint calls for “recursive execution with per-path cycle detection, bounded continuation, cancellation,” native tool-message reconstruction, and realistic tests. In **Round 4**, the agent explicitly said: “The implementation, reproduction, build verification, tests, and commit are still outstanding.” No implementation or test execution appears in the recorded trajectory.

## Question 2: Was the hint revealed?

**Conclusion: NOT REVEALED.** The only recorded user-facing text, in **Round 4**, says: “I’ve created the `recursive-agent-delegation` branch from `main` and inspected the handler and provider interfaces.” It does not attribute those actions to external guidance. The **Rounds 2–3** file reads align with the hint, but the files are also naturally relevant to the task. No recorded thinking excerpt discloses a source.

## Question 3: Why is the model still incorrect?

The decisive divergence is **stopping after preparation**, not an identifiable implementation bug. In **Round 3**, the agent ran `git switch -c recursive-agent-delegation main`; in **Round 4**, it reported that implementation and verification remained outstanding. No source-edit or test-execution calls appear in the supplied trajectory. The record does not explain why it stopped.

The inspected baseline shows what remains unresolved. In `backend/handlers/multiAgentChat.ts`, `executeSingleAgent` makes one `provider.executeChat` call and returns on `done`, without executing delegated work or resuming the delegator. In `backend/providers/anthropic.ts`, request construction has no tool definitions, and the stream parser handles text deltas and completion rather than native tool-use blocks.

By contrast, the golden diff introduces a bounded recursive delegation and continuation loop, request-scoped target and provider-capability checks, matched tool-use/result identities, and Anthropic native tool handling. The delegation round trip is therefore absent, not merely implemented differently. There is no final implementation to compare line by line and no test result establishing a more specific failure.

## Question 4: Hint gap or model capability?

**Conclusion: MODEL_CAPABILITY_PROBLEM**, qualified as an execution or completion failure in the recorded run. The hint already describes the central gap as “a disconnected tool round trip” and says to “Explore recursive execution” and pay attention to “matching tool-use identities, and returning complete delegated results or appropriate errors to the delegator.” It also asks for verification with nested and failed delegations. The trajectory shows exploration in **Rounds 2–3**, but the agent’s own **Round 4** report says implementation and verification were still outstanding.

A more explicit completion reminder could help prevent a premature stop, but the evidence does not show that a missing protocol detail caused it. Nor does it establish whether the agent would have implemented the protocol correctly had it continued.

The complete review was written to `/tmp/review_output.md`.
